text.en: The longest road trip in the world, from Talon in Russia to Sagres in Portugal, is 15,150 km. Within India, the North-South Corridor of 2019 ran from Srinagar to Kanniyakumari. How long was it? We add to find out.

To add large numbers, keep the digits lined up: ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds and thousands under thousands.
A place on the corridor is 1,855 km from Srinagar and 1,862 km from Kanniyakumari. Add: 5 + 2 = 7 ones, 5 + 6 = 11 tens, so write 1 and regroup 1 hundred, and so on. The total is 3,717 km.
When ten of one place is collected, we regroup it into one of the next place. Ten tens make one hundred.
The same method works for 5-digit numbers. Mahesh spent Rs 21,880 on fuel and toll and Rs 38,900 on other expenses: 21,880 + 38,900 = Rs 60,780.
To subtract, line up the digits and regroup when the top digit is smaller. A ship sails 2,700 km from Mumbai to Chennai by sea. After 1,083 km it reaches Cochin, so 2,700 - 1,083 = 1,617 km are left.
Check a subtraction by adding back: 1,617 + 1,083 should be 2,700.
Addition and subtraction are partners. If 46 + 21 = 67, then 67 - 21 = 46 and 67 - 46 = 21.
The book also plays with sums of consecutive numbers: the sum of 3 consecutive numbers is 3 times the middle number, so 67 + 68 + 69 = 3 x 68 = 204.
